Yes, such a family exists. This is the standard smooth cutoff (bump) function construction.

**Proof.**

We construct $\eta_R$ explicitly. The key ingredient is a one-dimensional $C^\infty$ (hence $C^1$) transition function. Define

$$
\psi(t) = 
\begin{cases}
0, & t \le 0,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{f(t)}{f(t)+f(1-t)}, & 0 < t < 1,\\[4pt]
1, & t \ge 1,
\end{cases}
\qquad\text{where}\qquad
f(s) = 
\begin{cases}
e^{-1/s}, & s > 0,\\
0, & s \le 0.
\end{cases}
$$

Since $f \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $f \ge 0$ and $f(t)+f(1-t) > 0$ on $(0,1)$, the function $\psi$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R}$, nondecreasing, with $\psi = 0$ on $(-\infty, 0]$ and $\psi = 1$ on $[1, \infty)$.

Now set, for $x \in \mathbb{R}^N$ with $r = |x|$,

$$
\eta_R(x) = 1 - \psi\!\left(\frac{r - R}{R}\right) = \psi\!\left(\frac{2R - r}{R}\right).
$$

Equivalently, $\eta_R(x) = \psi\!\bigl(\tfrac{2R - |x|}{R}\bigr)$. Let us verify each required property.

**Range $0 \le \eta_R \le 1$.** Since $0 \le \psi \le 1$ everywhere, the same holds for $\eta_R$.

**$\eta_R = 1$ on $B_R(0)$.** If $|x| \le R$, then $\tfrac{2R-|x|}{R} \ge 1$, so $\psi = 1$, hence $\eta_R(x) = 1$.

**$\eta_R = 0$ outside $B_{2R}(0)$.** If $|x| \ge 2R$, then $\tfrac{2R-|x|}{R} \le 0$, so $\psi = 0$, hence $\eta_R(x) = 0$.

**Compact support and regularity.** The support of $\eta_R$ is contained in $\overline{B_{2R}(0)}$, which is compact, so $\eta_R \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^N) \subset C_c^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.

**Gradient estimate.** By the chain rule,

$$
\nabla \eta_R(x) = \psi'\!\left(\frac{2R - |x|}{R}\right) \cdot \nabla\!\left(\frac{2R - |x|}{R}\right) = \psi'\!\left(\frac{2R - |x|}{R}\right) \cdot \left(-\frac{x}{R\,|x|}\right).
$$

Therefore

$$
|\nabla \eta_R(x)| = \frac{1}{R}\left|\psi'\!\left(\frac{2R - |x|}{R}\right)\right|.
$$

The derivative $\psi'$ is continuous and supported in $[0,1]$, hence bounded: there exists $M = \|\psi'\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})} < \infty$. Setting $C = M$ (a fixed constant depending only on the choice of $\psi$, not on $R$), we obtain

$$
|\nabla \eta_R(x)| \le \frac{C}{R} \quad \text{for all } x \in \mathbb{R}^N.
$$

Thus the family $\{\eta_R\}_{R>0}$ satisfies all the required properties with a constant $C$ independent of $R$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
